open_questions: Read Record Play Pause (2019) and Fast Forward (2020) for his own account of each part: only reports of them were read.
She's Lost Control's synth drum: Mixdown calls it a Synare, Wikipedia says he bought a Syndrum during the sessions. Which, and played how?
Dead Souls: the one human tab (Songsterr 39993, 2023) writes the toms and snare with no kick at all; check it against the record before modelling it.
The New Order years after 1983 (Blue Monday's Oberheim DMX, Temptation, the live kit) are not modelled; Blue Monday's sixteenth kick run is a machine's, which the critic would refuse from a foot.
Which drummers name him as an influence in their own words: none was found.
The kit's colour and maker after 1979, and whether the Rogers had single-headed concert toms as the tab's track name and the Something Else film suggest.

identity.name: Stephen Morris
identity.summary: Joy Division's drummer from August 1977 and New Order's ever since: a drummer who wanted to sound like a machine, after Klaus Dinger, Jaki Liebezeit and Moe Tucker, and who, under Martin Hannett, recorded one drum at a time. Straight, unvarying bars held for a whole song, the kick often on every beat, the hat in sixteenths around the snare, tom riffs in place of a backbeat; and from 1979 synth drums, then drum machines he programmed himself.

traditions.impact: Klaus Dinger of Neu! for his 'machine-like' playing; Jaki Liebezeit of Can, who 'kept it simple'.

formative_events.event: Answered Warsaw's advertisement for a drummer in August 1977, the only one who did, after Terry Mason, Tony Tabac and Steve Brotherdale.
Bought a synth drum after taking the device on the UK sleeve of Can's Tago Mago for one on Jaki Liebezeit's drums.

eras.label: Joy Division
eras.context: Warsaw, then Joy Division, with Martin Hannett: Unknown Pleasures (April 1979), Transmission, Love Will Tear Us Apart, Closer (March 1980).
defining_traits: one bar or pair for a whole song
the hat in sixteenths around the snare

eras.label: New Order
eras.context: Drums with sequencers and drum machines he programmed: Ceremony (1981), Power, Corruption & Lies (1983).

evidence.note: 'Machine-like' (after Dinger); Sumner: 'Steve wouldn't be the clock, because he's passive: he would follow the rhythm of the band.'

swing.notes: Straight eighths and sixteenths in every tab read.

dynamics.balance: Few accents and no ghosts in the tabs; the dynamics are in the production.

feel_profile.interaction: Locked to Hook's melodic bass rather than leading; the same bar for a song while the band moves over it.

hand_techniques.name: Sixteenths on the hat around the backbeat
hand_techniques.description: Both hands on the hat in sixteenths, the snare hand leaving it for 2 and 4 (Love Will Tear Us Apart, Transmission, Ceremony).

hand_techniques.name: Tom riffs
hand_techniques.description: A riff on the toms in place of a backbeat (Atrocity Exhibition), after Kenny Morris's playing mostly on toms.

foot_techniques.name: Four on the floor
foot_techniques.description: The kick on every beat (Love Will Tear Us Apart, Ceremony, Age of Consent).

Wikipedia: Stephen Morris, Joy Division, Unknown Pleasures, Closer, Atrocity Exhibition, Love Will Tear Us Apart, Ceremony, Power, Corruption & Lies

devices_search.note: None found. Every tab is 4/4 on the sixteenth grid; Twenty Four Hours' verse leaves the kick off 1 and puts the snare on 1 and 4, a displaced pair inside one meter with no cross pulse; Atrocity Exhibition is an ostinato, not a polyrhythm.

voice_language.snare: 2 and 4, often the only snare in the bar; rolls in fills (Shadowplay); none at all in Atrocity Exhibition.
voice_language.kick: On every beat, or on 1, its "and" and 3; never busy.
voice_language.toms: Riffs and runs down the kit in sixteenths (She's Lost Control, Atrocity Exhibition).
voice_language.hihat: Sixteenths with gaps for the snare, or eighths, opened on the "and"s; Shadowplay's open quarters.
voice_language.cymbals: Few: a crash at the top of a phrase; the ride in sixteenths on New Dawn Fades.

sound_profile.cymbal_character: Super Zyn hats and an Earth ride on Unknown Pleasures; sparing.

by_era.description: A Rogers concert kit with a Gretsch snare, recorded one drum at a time by Hannett, with AMS digital delay in the studio; a synth drum on She's Lost Control and Atrocity Exhibition.
Drums under sequencers and drum machines.

sample_hints.70s: Dead, dry toms and snare, every drum separate, a short gated room on it.
sample_hints.80s: A clean studio kit beside drum machines.

signature_traits.label: Machine-like
signature_traits.description: Straight, unvarying bars held for a whole song, played to sound like a machine: what he credits Klaus Dinger for.

signature_traits.label: One drum at a time
signature_traits.description: Martin Hannett had him play each drum on its own, for separation; Love Will Tear Us Apart's snare went on last, at 4 a.m.

signature_traits.label: Tom riffs
signature_traits.description: A riff on the toms with no snare or cymbal (Atrocity Exhibition), after Kenny Morris, in whose band 'the sound of cymbals was forbidden'.

signature_traits.label: Sixteenths round the backbeat
signature_traits.description: The hat in sixteenths with gaps for the snare on 2 and 4 (Transmission, Love Will Tear Us Apart, Ceremony).

signature_traits.label: Synth drums and machines
signature_traits.description: A synth drum from the Unknown Pleasures sessions; a Synare 3, a Simmons SDS4 and a Roland CR-78; electronic drums on four of Closer's tracks.

patterns.name: Disorder: the two-bar groove
patterns.function: Eighths on the closed hat, then the hat opened on the 'and' of 1 and of 2 and half-open on 3, the hat foot on 2; the kick on 1, its 'and', 3 and its 'and', then on the 'and' of 2; a second snare on the 'and' of 4

evidence.note: Songsterr's verse bars, alternating x8 each in every verse; tempo beat-tracked from the 2007 remaster (172.2).

patterns.name: Shadowplay: open quarters
patterns.function: Open hats in quarters, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1 and 3; every fourth bar a snare roll

evidence.note: The tab writes this bar 91 times of 139.

patterns.name: She's Lost Control: the one bar
patterns.function: The kick on 1, its 'and', the 'and' of 2 and 3, the snare on 2 and 4; on 1 and its 'and' a synth drum's hiss (GM 28 in the tab), not in these lanes

evidence.note: The tab writes this bar in every section; the synth drum is from Mixdown and the Syndrum story from Wikipedia.

patterns.name: New Dawn Fades: the ride in sixteenths
patterns.function: The ride in sixteenths, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1, the 'a' of 1, the 'and' of 2, 3 and its 'e', the 'a' of 3, the 'e' and 'a' of 4

patterns.name: Transmission: the two-bar pair
patterns.function: The hat in sixteenths with gaps for the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1, 3 and its 'and'; then the kick on 1, 3 and 4, the hat opened in pairs on 3 and 4, a second snare on their 'and's

evidence.note: The tab's commonest pair; the style plays the hat in threes to reach 158.

patterns.name: Atrocity Exhibition: the tom riff
patterns.function: No snare and no cymbal: three on the high tom from the 'and' of 1, the mid tom on the 'and' of 2 and from 3, the floor tom on 4 and its 'and', the kick on 1 and 3, the hat foot on 2 and 4

evidence.note: One bar for every bar of drums in the tab; the record beat-tracks at 128.6.

patterns.name: Twenty Four Hours: the verse
patterns.function: No kick on 1: eighths on the hat, open on the 'and' of 2, the snare on 1 and 4, the kick on the 'and' of 2 and 3; then the cross-stick on the 'and' of 1, 2 and its 'and', the kick on 3 and the 'and' of 4

evidence.note: The verse pair, x30 and x29 in the tab.

patterns.name: Love Will Tear Us Apart: the groove
patterns.function: The kick on every beat, the hat in sixteenths with a gap for the snare on 2 and 4 and two open on the 'and' of 3

evidence.note: The commonest bar in every section of the tab.

patterns.name: Ceremony: the riff
patterns.function: The kick on every beat, the hat in sixteenths accented on 1, 2, the 'and' of 3 and the 'a' of 4, then the high tom on the 'and' of 3 and of 4 and the mid tom on 4; the snare on the 'a' of 4 every other bar

evidence.note: The intro, verse and riff bars of the tab; which 1981 recording the tab follows is not said.

patterns.name: Age of Consent: the pair
patterns.function: The kick on every beat, the hat on 1 and its 'e', 'and' and 'a' and from the 'and' of 2 to 3, the snare on 2 and 4, the floor tom on the 'and' of 4; then the snare on the 'and' of 3 and of 4

evidence.note: The tab's pair in every section; the style leaves out the 'a' of 1 to reach the record's tempo.

equipment.label: Rogers concert kit
equipment.layout_notes: Mixdown's list: a 14-inch Gretsch snare, 12, 13, 14 and 15-inch hanging toms, 15-inch Super Zyn hats, a 20-inch Earth ride, 18 and 14-inch Zildjian crashes. Two Songsterr tabs name it a 'Rodgers Concert' kit.

evidence.note: Mixdown's account, for the Unknown Pleasures sessions; the Earth ride is Paiste's.

equipment.label: Synth drums and drum machines
equipment.layout_notes: A synth drum bought during the Unknown Pleasures sessions; a Synare 3, a Simmons SDS4 and a Roland CR-78.

affiliations.name: New Order
affiliations.notes: He and Sumner are the only members on every album.

evidence.note: He credits Dinger's influence for his 'machine-like' skills.
With Moe Tucker, 'the ones who kept it simple'; the device he took for a synth drum on Tago Mago's sleeve.
His playing mostly on toms; Siouxsie and the Banshees, where the sound of cymbals was forbidden.
Warsaw fired Brotherdale after the July 1977 demos and advertised; Morris answered in August.

innovations: Played drums to sound like a machine, then layered synth drums and programmed machines with them, in post-punk.
common_misconceptions: That Hannett had him rebuild his kit on the studio roof for She's Lost Control: Mixdown, telling the story, calls it uncertain.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A dry, dead kit, every drum separate
generation_rules: One bar or a two-bar pair for a whole section; fills rare, at phrase ends.
The kick on every beat, or on 1, its "and" and 3.
The hat in sixteenths with gaps for the snare on 2 and 4, or eighths opened on the "and"s.
Tom riffs in place of a backbeat.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Neu!'s Klaus Dinger, Can's Jaki Liebezeit, Moe Tucker and the Banshees' Kenny Morris; then Martin Hannett's studio, and the drum machines.
